hero.purpose: The one-sentence role statement on home and the first-person headline on /about. Once per surface, at the top.

display.purpose: Heading level 1 at rest: kit page titles and index-page titles.

headline.purpose: Heading level 2: home and About section titles.

title.purpose: Card titles, heading level 4, compact chrome.

body.purpose: Default copy and card descriptions. 16px on mobile, 14px from sm; lead paragraphs hold 16px/1.75.

label.purpose: Buttons, field labels, nav items. Badges drop to 0.75rem.

mono.purpose: Dates, reading time, tech tags, code, and the spaced-caps labels (0.08em, uppercase).

shadows.name: resting-edge
shadows.purpose: Content cards, kit cards, tool tiles, float navbar and sidebar. The edge reads; the surface does not float.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: Popovers, modals, sheets, command menu: the only structural lift.

shadows.name: overlay-drop
shadows.purpose: Stacked under overlay-lift on floating overlays, with a muted ring.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Card light fade, rail bead return, arrow nudges: responses that settle fast.

motion.name: ease-out-cubic
motion.purpose: Work Rail scrub travel, slow enough that the bead visibly passes each node.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default state transitions in the kit (badge overlay, switch).

motion.name: duration-copy
motion.purpose: Copy / Share cross-fade to the check and 'Copied!'.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Default state change; card print settle-back.

motion.name: duration-print-drift
motion.purpose: Card print trailing the pointer light.

motion.name: duration-outline-trace
motion.purpose: Post Outline trace moving to the current section (ease-out quart).

motion.name: duration-rail-scrub
motion.purpose: Work Rail bead travel out; 260ms back home.

motion.name: glyph-engine-cycle
motion.purpose: The Glyph Engine's craft → obsession → craft loop: the site's one ambient motion.

narrative.overview:
This is the visual system for Tri Rizeki Rifandani's public portfolio app. The public surfaces do one job: say who this person is, then let a visitor scan the work. The layout is conventional on purpose — a wordmark topbar, a hero that states the role in one sentence, then stacked bordered cards for work, projects, and writing. Nothing asks the reader to learn a novel structure before they can read.

The machinery underneath is App Router, React Aria, PWA, SEO, and observability. Accessibility is product truth, not a coat of paint: React Aria focus rings, 44px touch targets, and forced-colors fallbacks are part of the craft. The Master Design at `/master-design` remains the kit proof surface and keeps the denser app-chrome density.

Visual rejections: marketing-landing spectacle, neon accents, skeuomorphism, decorative illustration, hover-lift theater, and leftover "bulletproof Next template" branding. The one sanctioned exception is the Glyph Engine in the home hero (see Components): it is made from the system's own mono face and tokens, it acts out the headline, and it is not illustration.
keyCharacteristics: One accent (Helm Teal). Status colors are machinery lights, not brand.
Roboto for headings, Quicksand for body, IBM Plex Mono for meta. Three faces, three jobs, no fourth.
Soft-rect 8px default. Pills only for badges, toggles, and circular icon buttons.
Hybrid depth: tone + hairline at rest; shadow only on overlays. Cards never lift.
Light and dark as equal citizens. Primary chroma does not shift.
16px body on mobile, 14px from `sm` up — except hero and lead paragraphs, which hold 16px/1.75 at every width.
One card silhouette, shared by projects and posts, on home and on both index pages. Work rows are the one public row without it: they hang off the work rail instead.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Helm Teal occupies ≤10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point. Never wash a whole view in primary.

rules.name: The Same-Signal Rule
rules.body: Helm Teal does not change chroma between light and dark. Only surfaces invert.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Not-Brand Rule
rules.body: Teal, vermillion, and amber never appear as decorative chrome. They mean a state.

rules.name: The Three-Face Rule
rules.body: Roboto heads, Quicksand reads, IBM Plex Mono counts. A face outside its job is a bug, and a fourth family does not exist.

rules.name: The One-Hero Rule
rules.body: The display-scale hero appears once per surface, at the top, and never below the fold. It states a fact about the person; it is not a section title that got promoted.

rules.name: The Lead-Holds Rule
rules.body: Body copy steps 16px → 14px at `sm`, except lead paragraphs, which hold 16px/1.75 at every width. Do not mix a third body size in one view.

rules.name: The One-Column Rule
rules.body: Public surfaces cap at 64rem and read top to bottom. Widening the column strands a card's meta from its title and leaves the hero beside empty canvas.

rules.name: The One-Shell Rule
rules.body: Public routes render through `SiteShell`. A page that assembles its own header or footer will drift from the others.

rules.name: The Preview-Then-Index Rule
rules.body: A home section that has an index shows at most three entries and links to it. Home introduces; the index enumerates. Work experience has no index route, so it is the one section that lists in full — if it ever grows one, it takes the three-entry cap with it.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only as a response to floating (overlay). A card hover washes its background and may light it; it never lifts, scales, or grows a shadow. The sheet stays on the canvas — what moves is the light on it and the print inside its frame.

rules.name: The Ring-Over-Glow Rule
rules.body: Focus and hover never use colored drop-shadows. Use a 2–3px ring at 20% Helm Teal (or the intent color).

rules.name: The Canvas-Only Rule
rules.body: Grain belongs to the canvas. Cards, chrome, and overlays stay smooth, so the texture reads as the surface content rests on and never as noise inside the content.

rules.name: The Mean-Luminance Rule
rules.body: The grain moves the canvas it sits on: it darkens the light canvas by about 2% on average and lightens the dark canvas by about the same, so both `--canvas` values are set away from the tone they render as (light `#f9f8f7`, dark `#151312`). Two checks re-open whenever `--grain-opacity` moves — text on the canvas against the composited value, and card-against-canvas separation, which in dark mode collapses if the grain lightens the canvas up to the card.

rules.name: The Soft-Rect Rule
rules.body: 8px is the default corner. Pills are for badges, tech tags, toggles, and circular icon buttons only.

rules.name: The One-Moment Rule
rules.body: The Glyph Engine is the only ambient motion on the site. A second one splits the attention it exists to hold. Other motion stays a response to the reader (card light, rail scrub, ID Badge spin, theme transition).

rules.name: The Rail-Is-Chronology Rule
rules.body: The rail belongs to work experience, which is the one home section ordered by time. Projects and writing are ranked, not dated — they stay a plain stack.

rules.name: The One-Card Rule
rules.body: Project and post cards share one silhouette and differ only in filling. A surface that needs a third card shape needs a different surface — and a row that is neither ranked nor navigable, like a work entry, needs no card at all.

rules.name: The Static-Work Rule
rules.body: A work entry is not a link. Do not give it hover affordances it cannot honor: no row wash, no card light, no pointer cursor. The pointer reads the rail (the scrub), never the row.

dos: Do keep Helm Teal rare (The One Voice Rule) and identical across themes (The Same-Signal Rule).
Do use React Aria focus rings (2px + 20% wash, Paper offset on buttons) as a visible craft detail.
Do default to 8px soft-rects and `shadow-xs` + Hairline on resting surfaces.
Do head in Roboto, read in Quicksand, count in IBM Plex Mono (The Three-Face Rule).
Do render every public route through `SiteShell` (The One-Shell Rule).
Do preview at most three entries on home for any section that has an index, and link to it (The Preview-Then-Index Rule).
Do put public copy in `messages/en.json` and `messages/id.json`; leave names, titles, and prose content in `core/constants/portfolio.ts`.
Do put status only in Note, Badge, validation, and meter/progress — never as a decorative wash.
donts: Don't introduce a second brand hue or a fourth font family.

Don't lift cards or buttons on hover (`translateY`, card scale, colored drop-shadows, skeuomorphic bevels). Lighting a card and drifting its print inside a fixed frame are not lift — the card's own box never moves.
Don't paint marketing-landing spectacle, neon, or illustration into chrome.
Don't repeat the display-scale hero below the first screen.
Don't hardcode public-facing English in a component.
Don't brand the UI as a generic Next.js template.
Don't fabricate end-user brand claims, testimonials, or a WCAG certification level.
